observations: Photo 0 shows a swivel office chair with a fabric/mesh-looking back and a padded seat.
The chair has a silver metal base with 5 legs and caster wheels.
The seat and arm area look intact in the photo; no obvious torn fabric is visible.
The seller’s text says “Bent office chair,” but the photo does not clearly show a bent frame or bent legs.

claims.claim: Bent office chair available for sale.
claims.evidence: Photo 0 does not clearly show the bending; the frame/legs are not shown from angles that confirm a bend.
No photo evidence of the location (Opebi) is visible.

risks.risk: The chair may be bent in a way that affects stability (wobble) or alignment, which is not confirmable from this single angle.
risks.proof: A short video from the side and front showing the chair on a flat floor while someone gently rocks it, plus a close-up of the base/legs for any permanent bend.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as damaged/possibly not stable (worst case: needs repair or unsafe to use).

risks.risk: Caster wheels or the base may be damaged (cracked stem, bent wheel mounts), causing uneven rolling.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of all 5 casters and the underside of the base; then a clip showing the chair rolling smoothly in a straight line.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as if casters/base may need replacement.

risks.risk: Height adjustment (gas lift) may be faulty or weak, which cannot be tested from the photo.
risks.proof: A clip showing the lever being pressed and the seat height changing smoothly, then holding position without sinking.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as if height adjustment may not work.

risks.risk: Back/tilt mechanism may be loose or not functioning.
risks.proof: A clip showing the tilt/recline movement (if present) and that it locks/returns properly.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as if tilt/locking is not reliable.

proof_requests: Front + side video on a flat floor showing whether the chair wobbles/rocks (to confirm the “bent” claim).
Close-up photos of the underside/base and all 5 legs/casters.
Video of height adjustment working smoothly and holding position.
Video of any tilt/recline mechanism (if present) and whether it locks/returns properly.
reading.reason: The seller claims the chair is bent, but the single photo does not clearly confirm the damage or its severity. Without proof of stability/adjustment/tilt condition, a worst-case price cannot be set confidently.

observations: Photo 0 shows a UPS with the brand text “BLUE GATE” on the front panel.
Photo 0 shows a front power button and several indicator LEDs (exact labels not fully readable).
Photo 1 shows the UPS from the side/rear area with two-pin plug/cord connection visible at the top.
No visible model number, battery capacity (Ah), or watt/VA rating on the photos provided.

claims.evidence: Photo 0 and photo 1 clearly show a UPS unit.

risks.risk: Unknown battery health/remaining runtime; UPS may not hold charge even if it powers on.
risks.proof: Ask for a video showing the UPS running on battery after unplugging mains (e.g., 5–10 minutes) with the battery/indicator LEDs changing, plus a runtime estimate.
risks.if_unproven: Price it as battery not reliable / short runtime (worst case: treat as needing battery replacement).

risks.risk: Unknown capacity (VA/W) and number/type of outlets; affects what loads it can run.
risks.proof: Ask for a clear photo of the label/sticker showing VA/W rating and model number (usually on the back/bottom).
risks.if_unproven: Price it at the lowest likely usable capacity for a generic small UPS (worst case for value).

risks.risk: Possible fault: inverter/charger may be weak; indicators may look normal but output may be unstable.
risks.proof: Ask for a photo/video of the UPS output under load (e.g., connect a small lamp or phone charger and show it stays on when mains is removed).
risks.if_unproven: Price it as not fully working for reliable backup (worst case: treat as needs repair).

risks.risk: Missing accessories/cables (battery leads, power cable, manual) or incorrect power cord.
risks.proof: Ask for a photo showing everything included: power cable, any manuals, and all output sockets.
risks.if_unproven: Price it assuming only the unit is included (worst case: buyer may need to source missing parts).

proof_requests: Clear close-up photo of the UPS rating label (VA/W, input/output, model number, serial if present) on back/bottom.
Video: UPS switched on and then mains unplugged to show it runs on battery (with indicator LEDs).
Video/photo: UPS connected to a small load (lamp/phone charger) to confirm stable output during battery mode.
Photo of included items: power cable/plug type and all ports/outlets.
reading.reason: The photos confirm it is a BLUE GATE UPS, but the key pricing factors (battery condition/runtime and exact VA/W capacity/model) are not readable. Without those, a safe worst-case price cannot be determined.

observations: Photo shows a dark screen TV with visible glare/reflection; no clear screen content.
No readable brand/model label is visible in the photo.
No clear view of the back panel, ports, power button, or any damage details.

claims.claim: A 29-inch LG TV is for sale.
claims.evidence: Photo 0 does not show any readable LG branding or the screen size.

claims.claim: It’s the transformer that got blown up.
claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows no internal/back view or component-level evidence; transformer failure cannot be confirmed remotely.

claims.claim: Location: Onike, near the University of Lagos (Unilag), Lagos State.
claims.evidence: No location evidence in the photo.

risks.risk: TV may have more than transformer damage (e.g., power supply board, main board, backlight/LED driver, panel damage).
risks.proof: A short video of the TV attempting to power on (standby light behavior) plus a clear photo of the back cover/label and any visible burnt parts on the power board.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not working / parts-only until proven otherwise.

risks.risk: Screen/panel may be damaged (no image, lines, or backlight issues).
risks.proof: Video showing power-on with brightness/backlight visible (even if no picture) and a close-up of the screen for lines/spotting.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not working / no guarantee of display.

risks.risk: Brand/model and exact size may be different from what’s claimed, affecting parts availability and value.
risks.proof: Photo of the TV’s rear label showing LG model number and screen size.
risks.if_unproven: Priced at worst-case generic broken TV value without assuming LG/29-inch.

risks.risk: Possible scam/incorrect item (photos don’t confirm the claimed model or fault).
risks.proof: Photo of the exact TV with a visible label + a photo of the power board area (back cover removed) showing the suspected transformer/power section.

proof_requests: Clear photo of the rear label (LG model number + screen size).
Photo of the back cover and power supply area (showing the transformer/power board).
Short video: plug in, power on, show standby light and any backlight/power behavior.
Close-up photo of the screen (for lines/spotting) and ports (to confirm completeness).
reading.reason: From photo 0, the TV’s brand/model/size and the claimed transformer-only fault are not verifiable. With no proof of what’s actually damaged, the safest pricing requires confirmation via rear label and power-on/backlight behavior.
